claim: McCallum and Nigam distinguish multivariate Bernoulli from multinomial event models for text classification
locator: Abstract; Introduction; Probabilistic Framework of Naive Bayes
notes: Bernoulli models occurrences and absences; multinomial models counts

claim: The 1998 paper compares both event models on five corpora and reports mean 27 percent relative error reduction for multinomial over Bernoulli in its experimental setting
notes: Historical experimental average, not a universal or present-day expected gain

claim: The 1998 paper observes Bernoulli competitive at smaller vocabularies but multinomial generally stronger at larger vocabularies
notes: Scope limited to corpus and vocabulary configurations in paper

claim: The Bayesian classifier can be optimal under zero-one classification loss despite violations of conditional independence in some settings
notes: Do not conflate decision optimality with posterior probability calibration

claim: Later work identifies weaknesses in multinomial naive Bayes assumptions and proposes text-classification improvements
notes: Rennie et al 2003 is not the origin of naive Bayes

claim: Multinomial additive smoothing and Bernoulli absence term are standard modern parameterizations
locator: Multinomial Naive Bayes and Bernoulli Naive Bayes
notes: Alpha and feature encoding explicitly described

claim: Six-document example with V=8 and alpha=1 gives posterior odds promo/work 12 to 1 for free offer
locator: Independent example implementing the paper's multinomial event-model equations
notes: Promo and work both have 9 word tokens; free counts 3/0; offer counts 2/0; ratio 12, posterior 12/13

claim: Repeating a token changes multinomial scores but not Bernoulli scores for the same binary feature vector
locator: Paper event-model definitions; independent deterministic toy implementation
notes: Shown in interactive experiment and Python asserts
